scenario: Permafrost monitoring stations only flag methane emission events exceeding 200 mg/m²/day (alert threshold). Flagged events show a mean emission of 320 mg/m²/day (σ=55 mg/m²/day). Climate scientists want the true mean emission rate across all emission events.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming methane emission rate follows a normal distribution with σ=55 mg/m²/day, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 200] = 320. (b) What fraction of all methane emission rate events lie above the 200 mg/m²/day threshold? (c) By how much (in mg/m²/day) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 320 mg/m²/day is E[X|X>200], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=320 numerically yields μ=317.74508 mg/m²/day. Only 98.4% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 2.25492 mg/m²/day. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean methane emission rate is 320 mg/m²/day because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 200 mg/m²/day are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>200], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=200, σ=55. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 320 and solve for μ via brentq on [-1175.0, 319.9999]. (4) Solution: μ=317.74508 mg/m²/day. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((200−317.74508)/55)=0.98386.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 320,55,200
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-317.74508)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.98386)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-2.25492)<0.01
